title: Paleochemistry Extraction Lab
description: You are a paleochemist extracting ancient DNA from a mosquito preserved in amber. The amber specimen sits inside a heated coffee mug acting as a thermal dissolution vessel, and you must wear UV-filter sunglasses to safely observe fluorescent chemical reactions. Perform a multi-step extraction protocol by adjusting temperature, adding reagents, timing UV exposure, and isolating the DNA sample.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with ES modules from cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load three GLB assets: MosquitoInAmber.glb (centered on a lab bench), coffeeMug.glb (scaled up 2x as a thermal dissolution vessel positioned so the amber sits inside it), and SunglassesKhronos.glb (floating in the upper-left as a toggleable UV-filter overlay). Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0,3,5) with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (0.4), a directional light simulating lab overhead, and a point light inside the mug that changes color with temperature. Create an HTML overlay panel with controls and readouts. The 8-step interaction protocol: (1) Click a 'Power On' button to activate the thermal vessel — the mug's interior point light turns from gray to soft red. (2) Use a temperature slider (range 25-200°C) to heat the vessel to exactly 85-95°C — validate range, show temperature readout, mug light interpolates from blue(cold) through orange to red(hot). (3) Click 'Add Solvent' button to trigger a translucent green liquid plane rising inside the mug with an animation. (4) Toggle the sunglasses by clicking them — this applies a purple-tinted post-processing overlay (set scene background/fog to purple tint and add a vignette CSS overlay) representing UV filtering. Sunglasses model moves to screen-center when active. (5) With glasses ON, click 'UV Lamp' button to activate a purple PointLight above the amber — the amber mesh material emissive property pulses green to simulate fluorescence (only visible correctly with glasses on). (6) Use a timer input (validate 30-120 seconds) and click 'Incubate' �� show a countdown timer, during which the amber slowly becomes more transparent (adjust material opacity from 1.0 to 0.3). (7) Click 'Extract Sample' — animate a small glowing sphere (DNA) rising out of the amber and floating above the mug. (8) Click 'Analyze' — display a results panel showing mock spectral data (random wavelength peaks as an SVG bar chart) and a success message. Track completion of all 8 steps in order, disable out-of-order actions, and show a progress bar. Add parameter validation: temperature must be 85-95°C before solvent, glasses must be on before UV lamp, timer must be 30-120s.
